goodbye.note: Casual: Baai! To someone who is leaving: Mooi loop! (go well).

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: Baie dankie.

youre_welcome.note: Also common: Dis 'n plesier, or Nie te danke nie.

no.note: Sounds like 'near' without the r. 'Not' is nie.

sorry.note: Full form: Ek is jammer. Sorry is also used a lot.

excuse_me.note: Also very common: Ekskuus! or Ekskuus tog!

good_morning.note: Casual: Môre! The ô sounds like the 'aw' in 'law'.

how_are_you.note: U is the polite 'you'. Casual: Hoe gaan dit? or Hoe gaan dit met jou?

im_fine.note: Shorter: Goed, dankie. To ask back: En met u?

im_from.note: Also common: Ek kom uit … or Ek is van …

speak_english.note: Casual: Praat jy Engels? Most Afrikaans speakers also speak English.

dont_understand.note: Longer sentences take a double nie: Ek verstaan nie wat u sê nie.

speak_slowly.note: Softer: Kan u asseblief stadiger praat?

where.note: The w is said like v: 'vaar'. Where to? Waarheen?

what.note: Wat? alone can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say Ekskuus? or Sorry?

when.note: Stress on the second part: va-NEER.

who.note: Sounds like 'vee'. Whose? is Wie s'n?

how_much.note: Also very common: Wat kos dit?

where_bathroom.note: In someone's home, ask for die badkamer (the bathroom).

one.note: Sounds like 'ee-un'. Not the same as 'n (a, an), which is said like a short 'uh'.

three.note: Sounds like 'dree', with a rolled r.

four.note: The v is an f sound: 'feer'.

five.note: The y sounds like the 'ay' in 'say': 'fayf'.

seven.note: The w is a v sound: 'SEE-uh-vuh'.

eight.note: The g is throaty, like the ch in Scottish 'loch'.

water.note: Said 'VAH-tuhr': the w is a v sound and the r is pronounced. Tap water: kraanwater.

tea.note: Rooibostee (rooibos tea) is a South African favourite.

bread.note: A bread roll is a broodjie.

im_hungry.note: In speech often: Ek's honger. Very hungry: Ek is baie honger.

menu_please.note: Many people also say die menu. Politer: Kan ek die spyskaart kry, asseblief?

bill_please.note: Politer: Kan ek die rekening kry, asseblief?

delicious.note: Everyday favourite: Lekker! It works for food, weather and good times.

no_meat.note: Note the double nie. Also: Ek is 'n vegetariër.

right.note: Turn right: Draai regs. 'Correct' is reg, without the s.

straight_ahead.note: Keep going straight: Gaan reguit aan.

stop_here.note: Also common: Hou asseblief hier stil.

want_to_go.note: Very common in speech: Ek wil … toe gaan.

is_it_far.note: Is it a long walk? Is dit ver om te loop?

too_expensive.note: In speech usually: Dis te duur.

id_like_this.text: Ek wil graag hierdie een hê, asseblief
id_like_this.note: Also common: Ek sal hierdie een vat (I'll take this one).

just_looking.note: Also: Ek kyk maar net rond.

cash.note: To pay in cash: kontant betaal.

closed.note: Sounds like 'too'. Formal signs may say Gesluit.

yesterday.note: The g is throaty, like the ch in Scottish 'loch'.

now.note: Careful: nou-nou means 'in a little while'. Right now: nou dadelik.

later.note: Said 'LAH-tuhr', with the r pronounced. Also very common: netnou (in a while).

good_night.note: Casual: Nag! When going to bed: Lekker slaap!

see_you_later.note: Also: Tot later! or just Sien jou!

wait_moment.note: Also: Net 'n oomblik, asseblief. Casual: Wag gou!

call_police.note: In South Africa the police emergency number is 10111.

dont_feel_well.note: Lekker here means 'well'. Also: Ek is siek (I'm ill).

allergic.note: Example: Ek is allergies vir neute (nuts).

no_problem.note: The final nie is the Afrikaans double negative. Casual: Dis reg! (That's fine).

dont_know.note: Also: Ek het geen idee nie (I have no idea).

i_like_it.note: For food or something you enjoy: Dis lekker!

im_happy.note: Glad or pleased right now: Ek is bly.

congratulations.note: On a birthday: Veels geluk met jou verjaarsdag!

my_family.note: Familie is the wider family. Your own household (parents and children) is your gesin.

mother.note: The everyday word: my ma. Formal or written: moeder. Small children say mamma.

father.note: The everyday word: my pa. Formal or written: vader. Small children say pappa. Parents: ouers.

brother.note: Plural: broers. The oe sounds like the 'oo' in 'food'.

sister.note: Plural: susters. In hospitals, Suster is also how you address a nurse.

child.note: Plural: kinders. Son: seun. Daughter: dogter.

friend.note: A female friend: vriendin. Casual: maat or pel (mate, buddy).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: Dit is my vriendin. To rule out 'partner': Dit is 'n vriend (or vriendin) van my.

monday.note: Days are always capitalised in Afrikaans. On Monday: op Maandag, or just Maandag.

tuesday.note: The final g is throaty, like the ch in Scottish 'loch': 'DINS-dakh'.

wednesday.note: The w is a v sound and oe sounds like 'oo': 'VOONS-dakh'.

thursday.note: From donder (thunder), just like English Thursday (Thor's day).

friday.note: The y sounds like the 'ay' in 'say': 'FRAY-dakh'.

weekend.note: Have a lovely weekend: Lekker naweek!

what_day.note: For the date: Wat is die datum vandag?

next_week.note: Last week: verlede week. This week: hierdie week.

twelve.note: Said 'twahlf'. 13 to 19 end in -tien: dertien, veertien.

twenty.note: 21 is een-en-twintig: the units come first, as in 'one-and-twenty'.

thousand.note: Also: eenduisend. The ui is roughly the 'ay' in 'say', said with rounded lips.

years_old.note: Jaar stays singular after a number: Ek is dertig jaar oud. Often just: Ek is dertig.

green.note: Throaty g, and oe sounds like 'oo': 'khroon'.

what_colour.note: Casual: Wat se kleur is dit?

this_one.note: Also: dié een, with the stress on dié.

that_one.note: In speech usually shortened: daai een.

another_one.note: Naming the item: Nog 'n koffie, asseblief.

its_hot.note: Warm covers 'hot' for weather. In speech: Dis warm! Scorching: Dis snikheet.

its_cold.note: In speech: Dis koud! Freezing: Dis yskoud.

its_raining.note: The ë splits the word into two syllables: re-ën.

its_sunny.note: Also: Dis sonnig. The y sounds like the 'ay' in 'say': 'skayn'.

its_windy.note: Literally 'it's blowing'. Also: Dis winderig. Very windy: Dit waai kwaai.

weather_today.note: Also very common: Hoe lyk die weer vandag?

beautiful_day.note: Warmer: Wat 'n pragtige dag! In speech dit is usually becomes dis.

summer.note: In summer: in die somer. In South Africa, summer is December to February.

winter.note: Same word as English, but said 'VIN-tuhr'. In South Africa, winter is June to August.

have_reservation.note: Also: Ek het 'n kamer bespreek (I booked a room).

passport.note: Your passport, please: U paspoort, asseblief.

luggage.note: Throaty g: 'buh-KHAH-see'. A suitcase is a tas.

wifi_password.text: Wat is die wagwoord vir die Wi-Fi?
wifi_password.note: Wagwoord is password. Wi-Fi is said as in English; many people write wifi.

check_out_time.note: Checking in is inboek. Many people also just say uitcheck.

bus.note: The same word as English. Bus stop: bushalte.

next_train.note: Also: Hoe laat vertrek die volgende trein?

is_this_seat_free.note: A seat is a sitplek. Also very common: Sit hier iemand? (Is anyone sitting here?)

what_do_you_do.note: Casual: Wat werk jy? On forms, occupation is beroep.

i_work_in.note: For a company or workplace use by: Ek werk by 'n bank.

im_student.note: A woman says the same. A school pupil is a leerder.

meeting.note: Said 'fuhr-KHAH-duh-ring'. In speech many people also just say meeting.

im_busy.note: Said 'BEE-sukh'. Very busy: Ek is baie besig.

day_off.note: In speech often: Ek is môre af (I'm off tomorrow). A day of leave from work: 'n verlofdag.

colleague.note: Same word for a woman. Plural: kollegas.

lets_start.note: Also: Laat ons begin (a little more formal).

good_job.note: Also: Goed gedoen! or Knap gedoen!

table_for_two.note: Politer: Kan ons 'n tafel vir twee kry, asseblief?

what_recommend.note: Casual: Wat sal jy aanbeveel? Also: Wat is lekker hier?

not_spicy.note: Note the double nie. Only mild: Nie te pittig nie, asseblief.

more_water.note: Politer: Kan ons nog water kry, asseblief?

no_sugar.note: With milk but no sugar: met melk, sonder suiker.

im_full.note: Politer at the table: Ek is versadig, dankie. Casual: Ek het my dik geëet.

takeaway.note: Also: Om saam te neem. Takeaways: wegneemetes.

keep_change.note: Maar softens it, like 'just'. A tip is 'n fooitjie.

head_hurts.note: Seer means sore. Also: Ek het hoofpyn.

call_ambulance.note: In South Africa the ambulance number is 10177.

dentist.note: Tand is tooth, arts is doctor. Toothache: tandpyn.

need_rest.note: Also: Ek het rus nodig. Going to lie down: Ek gaan 'n bietjie lê.

feel_better.note: Also: Dit gaan beter met my.

get_well.note: Fuller: Ek hoop jy voel gou beter!

lets_meet.note: Kry mekaar is the everyday way to say meet up. Also: Kom ons spreek iets af (let's arrange something).

are_you_free.note: Casual: Is jy môre vry? Also: Het jy môre tyd?

call_me.note: Casual: Gee my 'n luitjie! (give me a ring).

your_number.note: Casual: Wat is jou nommer? Cellphone number: selnommer.

see_you_soon.note: Also: Tot gou! or Sien jou binnekort.

have_nice_day.note: Casual: Lekker dag! Later in the day: Lekker dag verder!

good_luck.note: Also: Alles van die beste! Careful: Baie geluk! means congratulations.

happy_birthday.note: Short: Veels geluk! To someone older: met u verjaarsdag. Also heard: Gelukkige verjaarsdag!

thanks_a_lot.note: Even warmer: Baie, baie dankie! Formal: Hartlik dank.

miss_you.note: Also very common and warmer: Ek verlang na jou.
